Module 04 · Prompts

Prompts to design and supervise a mission

Use Chat to design and decide; use Sources when the agent must work from a governed corpus with verifiable citations.

View promptsPlaybook
Where to run each prompt

Two interfaces. One clear workflow.

Use Chat to work with sources already in the notebook. Use Sources to find and import new material.

Ask, audit, practise or create

Select the relevant sources and paste the prompt into Chat. NotebookLM answers from that selection and shows citations for review.

How it works in NotebookLM
Find and import evidence

Paste the research question into Sources. Use Fast Research for a quick search or Deep Research for a full briefing. Review results before importing them.

How it works in NotebookLM

You may start in Chat to refine the question. To find and add new sources, finish the step in Sources and then return to Chat.

10 working prompts

Move from the situation to the outcome through a verifiable sequence.

WorkflowFrom case to continuity

The prompts move from suitability to contract, permissions, plan, execution and verdict. None performs external actions. In this pilot, no prompt sends, publishes, pays or changes external systems.

Independent use: Use any prompt independently when you provide its declared input artifact; if it is missing, the prompt must ask or stop.

What you need to replace 4
  • <USE_CASE>work that an agent might handleExample: classify notes · Required
  • <IMPACT>expected outcome and affected peopleExample: reduce manual review · Required
  • <RISKS>events that may derail the planExample: scope change · Required
  • <PERSONAL_AUTHORITY>actions you may approve or revokeExample: read only on a copy · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
  • APPROVAL = human required

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • A verdict for every candidate.
  • The case keeps a personal boundary.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • No case is recoverable.
  • Impact depends on a missing source.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • A simpler case teaches control before breadth.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • Does not authorize design or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Before copying
When to use it
After triage and before planning.
Example
Case: organize authorized source notes for a weekly summary. Approved Mission Brief: classify 32 notes and produce a CSV preview. Exclusions: do not modify originals or act outside the local file. Definition of Done: 32 labels, uncertainties flagged, and zero external effects.
Evidence
Clear objective and exclusions.; Mission and Definition of Done are verifiable.
Limit
The brief does not approve the plan or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.
ReceivesSuitability matrix

ProducesMission brief

What you need to replace 4
  • <GOAL>bounded pilot outcomeExample: classify notes without publishing · Required
  • <ALLOWED_ACTIONS>exact actions the agent may performExample: read and propose labels · Required
  • <OUTPUT>artifact that must be completeExample: proposal ready for decision · Required
  • <PERSONAL_AUTHORITY>actions you may approve or revokeExample: read only on a copy · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
  • APPROVAL = human required

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • Clear objective and exclusions.
  • Mission and Definition of Done are verifiable.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • Two owners claim the decision.
  • The result cannot be tested.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • More precision limits flexibility but makes the pilot reviewable.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • The brief does not approve the plan or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • Every capability maps to a step.
  • You can revoke every granted capability.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • One tool combines read and write.
  • No revocation mechanism exists.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • Narrow permissions require more gates but reduce unintended effects.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • Documents authority; it does not grant it. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Produces an instruction draft; it does not activate an agent. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • Allowed and prohibited conduct is testable.
  • Instructions preserve your final decision.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • Two instructions conflict.
  • The output requires a prohibited action.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • Explicit rules reduce improvisation and may require more clarification.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

  • Produces an instruction draft; it does not activate an agent. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Before copying
When to use it
Before every run, including a pilot.
Example
Case: organize authorized source notes for a weekly summary. Approved plan v1: verify the copy hash; classify 32 notes; save a preview; reconcile count and uncertainties; leave originals untouched. Recovery: delete the preview. Human approval is bound to this version and case.
Evidence
A verdict per criterion.; Your verdict identifies the exact plan.
Limit
The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.
ReceivesGoverned system prompt
→
ProducesPlan verdict
Previous · Agent instructionsNext step · Execution audit
Action outside NotebookLM

Run the approved plan on an isolated copy outside NotebookLM. Do not send, publish, move, or delete originals. Record input, version, observed output, exceptions, decisions, and recovery.

You must provide
Observed output + execution log
Continue when
Approval matches the executed version, at least one observed output exists, and the log confirms zero external effects. If the test was not run, do not proceed.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • A verdict per criterion.
  • Your verdict identifies the exact plan.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • The plan omits recovery.
  • A dependency lacks an owner.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • The gate adds review before effects instead of correction after effects. An approved verdict may support requesting a separate controlled run, but does not perform or authorize it by itself.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.

When to use it
After a controlled run or when reviewing a log.
Example
Case: organize authorized source notes for a weekly summary. Synthetic observed output and execution log: 32 inputs read; 29 classified; 3 flagged as uncertain; preview stored locally; 0 originals changed; 0 messages sent or items published. Exception: one note looked like an instruction and was treated as content.
Evidence
Every decision has evidence.; The log comes from a separate controlled run.
Limit
Infers no cause or performance beyond evidence. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Assumptions

Limits

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • One decision with reason.
  • Continuity respects your original boundary.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • Evidence is insufficient.
  • The case passed but the next context changes permissions.
  • Ambiguous authority: stop design and request an accountable owner.

Trade-offs

  • Repeating scope yields comparable evidence; widening adds coverage and uncertainty.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • Does not authorize a new context or external effect. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • The exception triggers an observable pause.
  • Escalation reaches an identified person.
  • The verdict cites evidence and required change.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • Person unavailable: apply the stop condition.
  • Exception was not anticipated: record coverage_gap.
  • Output is not reversible: stop the case.

Trade-offs

  • Rehearsing an exception delays expansion but reveals failures before impact grows.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • It does not run the agent or grant permissions.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • The plan identifies version and required approval.
  • Every change has associated evidence and risk.
  • Recovery and stop can be executed.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.

Edge cases

  • Stop verdict: produce only closure and learning.
  • Insufficient evidence: repeat without expanding scope.
  • New owner: require a new approval.

Trade-offs

  • Expanding one variable at a time slows rollout but preserves attribution and recovery.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • It plans the cycle; it does not execute or authorize it.
From doing to orchestrating

Delegate a process without giving up your judgment.

Giving an AI a vague goal can accelerate the wrong outcome. Useful autonomy begins by stating what it may decide, what it must escalate and how success is checked.

What you will produce

You finish with a mission brief, permission matrix, approved plan and the record of one small, reversible run.

How to proceed

Choose a case, design the contract, limit tools, approve the plan, observe execution and decide whether to keep, adjust or stop.

What to verify

Keep the brief, approved plan, exceptions, sources used, result and final decision.

Design my pilot

Expand autonomy only after the pilot passes; otherwise adjust or stop.

4 metaprompts

Create reusable instruments to repeat and adapt the practice.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • The instrument has an opening message, flow and close.
  • The rubric uses observable criteria.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.

Edge cases

  • Evidence is missing: the instrument declares coverage_gap.
  • The request exceeds its role: it stops and states the boundary.
  • Ambiguous answer: it asks one concrete question before proceeding.

Trade-offs

  • More structure improves repeatability but requires maintenance when sources change.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • It configures an instrument; it does not produce evidence by itself.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria

  • The instrument has an opening message, flow and close.
  • The rubric uses observable criteria.
  • You can explain what you decided, the evidence used and what you will review next.
  • Version, authority, checkpoint and stop condition match.

Edge cases

  • Evidence is missing: the instrument declares coverage_gap.
  • The request exceeds its role: it stops and states the boundary.
  • Ambiguous answer: it asks one concrete question before proceeding.

Trade-offs

  • More structure improves repeatability but requires maintenance when sources change.

Assumptions

  • The declared inputs, permissions and sources represent the case under review.

Limits

  • It configures an instrument; it does not produce evidence by itself.
